_This page is generated from src/checks/, so it says what the tool does._

A check is one object in the `checks` list of a `case.json`. Every check has a `type`, and takes an optional `weight`, a positive number that defaults to 1. [Write a case](../guides/write-a-case.md) shows how to use them.

## Check types

| Check                 | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Scores 1 when                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `skill_loaded`        | optional `skill`, optional `anyOf`, optional `first`, optional `ignoring`. With `first: true` the first skill load must be a named skill, and no tool call that does not fit `ignoring` may come before it; every call of the run counts, a subagent's included, because calls cannot yet be told apart by the agent that made them. It takes exactly one of `skill` and `anyOf`, and `ignoring` only with `first`.                                                                                                                                               | The agent loaded that skill, or any of the skills in `anyOf`.                                                                                                                            |
| `skill_not_loaded`    | `skill`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | The agent did not load that skill.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `output_matches`      | `pattern`, optional `flags`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The final answer matches the regular expression.                                                                                                                                         |
| `output_lacks`        | `pattern`, optional `flags`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The final answer does not match the regular expression.                                                                                                                                  |
| `output_contains`     | `text`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The final answer contains that text.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `output_not_contains` | `text`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The final answer does not contain that text.                                                                                                                                             |
| `file_exists`         | `path`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | That file exists in the workspace after the run.                                                                                                                                         |
| `file_matches`        | `path`, `pattern`, optional `flags`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | That file exists and matches the regular expression.                                                                                                                                     |
| `tool_called`         | at least one of `kind`, `name`, optional `inputMatches`, optional `flags`, optional `min`, optional `max`, optional `sameTurn`, optional `first`. A count sees every call of the run, a subagent's included: calls cannot yet be told apart by the agent that made them. `sameTurn` needs a harness with `turnGrouping`; elsewhere the case is not applicable.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | The agent made tool calls that fit every given field, and their number is from `min` to `max`. With `sameTurn`, they were all issued in one assistant turn.                              |
| `tool_not_called`     | at least one of `kind`, `name`, optional `inputMatches`, optional `flags`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | The agent made no tool call that fits every given field.                                                                                                                                 |
| `first_tool`          | `matches`, optional `ignoring`. A subagent's calls are in the list too, because calls cannot yet be told apart by the agent that made them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The first tool call, once the calls that fit `ignoring` are dropped, fits `matches`.                                                                                                     |
| `tool_order`          | optional `before`, optional `after`, optional `sequence`, optional `strict`. It takes exactly one of the pair `before` and `after`, and `sequence`. With `strict: true` a sequence also forbids a later matcher's call before an earlier matcher's first match, and an earlier matcher's call after a later matcher's first match: `[researcher, synthesizer]` allows two researchers, then the synthesizer, and no researcher after it. The check sees every call of the run, a subagent's included: calls cannot yet be told apart by the agent that made them. | The calls come in the order given: with `before` and `after`, the chosen `before` call is earlier than the chosen `after` call; with `sequence`, the matchers match calls in that order. |
| `subject_unchanged`   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | The agent changed nothing in the copy of the subject that the run loaded.                                                                                                                |
| `judge`               | `rubric`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Not 0 or 1. A model scores the final answer against the rubric.                                                                                                                          |
| `decision`            | `question`, optional `expect`, optional `options`. It takes exactly one of `expect` and `options`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Not 0 or 1. A decision model gives each allowed answer a probability, and the score is the expected value.                                                                               |

## Fields

| Field           | Type       | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `skill`         | `text`     | The name of a skill.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `pattern`       | `regex`    | A regular expression.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `text`          | `text`     | Text to look for. The match is exact and case-sensitive.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `path`          | `path`     | A file path inside the workspace.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `kind`          | `kind`     | What the tool does, with the same word in every harness.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `name`          | `regex`    | A regular expression for the harness's own tool name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `inputMatches`  | `regex`    | A regular expression for the tool call's input, written as JSON.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `flags`         | `flags`    | The flags of the check's regular expressions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `anyOf`         | `texts`    | A list of skill names, any of which is accepted. Give this or `skill`, not both.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `min`           | `count`    | The fewest matching calls that pass: a whole number, 0 or more. Default: 1.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `max`           | `count`    | The most matching calls that pass: a whole number, 0 or more. Default: no limit.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `sameTurn`      | `bool`     | True to require every matching call to be issued in one assistant turn, so that `min` and `max` count calls that were launched together. A matching call with no turn fails it, unless it is the only match. Needs a harness with `turnGrouping`. Default: false.           |
| `first`         | `bool`     | True to require the first thing the agent did to be what the check names: for `tool_called`, the run's first tool call fits the matcher fields; for `skill_loaded`, the first skill load is the skill, and no tool call outside `ignoring` comes before it. Default: false. |
| `before`        | `matcher`  | The calls that must come first, as a matcher, with `which` for the first or last of them. Every call counts, a subagent's included.                                                                                                                                         |
| `after`         | `matcher`  | The calls that must come second, as a matcher, with `which` for the first or last of them. Every call counts, a subagent's included.                                                                                                                                        |
| `sequence`      | `matchers` | A list of matchers that must match calls in this order, with other calls allowed between them.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `strict`        | `bool`     | True for a `sequence` to forbid a later matcher's call before an earlier matcher's first match, and an earlier matcher's call after a later matcher's first match. Default: false.                                                                                          |
| `matches`       | `matcher`  | The matcher that the first tool call must fit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ignoring`      | `matchers` | Matchers for calls to leave out before looking at the first call, such as a read the agent is allowed to make first.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `rubric`        | `text`     | Plain text that says what a good answer does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `question`      | `text`     | A question about the final answer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `expect`        | `enum`     | The answer that scores 1 for a yes or no question: "yes" or "no".                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `options`       | `answers`  | An object of at least two answers, each with a number from 0 to 1 that says what the answer is worth.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `requires`      | `needs`    | A list of capabilities the check needs, such as `"mcp"`, or `"bin:<name>"` for an executable on the host's `PATH`. A harness that lacks one cannot run the check.                                                                                                           |
| `ifUnsupported` | `enum`     | What a harness that lacks what the check needs does: "skip" drops this check and re-normalizes the weights, "not-applicable" excludes the whole case. Default: "not-applicable".                                                                                            |

## Case file keys

The keys of a `case.json`. Any other key is a load error, except a key that starts with `x-` and `$schema`, a string that points an editor at [the schema](config.md#json-schemas).

| Key              | Type        | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checks`         | `object`    | A non-empty list of checks.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `weight`         | `number`    | How much the case counts in its suite. Default: 1.                                                                                                                                                |
| `minScore`       | `unit`      | The lowest score the case may get and still pass.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `maxTurns`       | `int`       | The most turns the agent may take. Only Claude Code applies it.                                                                                                                                   |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `int`       | The seconds a run may take. Default: 600.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `requires`       | `needs`     | A list of capabilities the case needs, such as `"mcp"`, or `"bin:<name>"` for an executable on the host's `PATH`. A harness that lacks one reports the case as not applicable.                    |
| `harnesses`      | `harnesses` | The harness ids the case is for. Any other harness reports it as not applicable. Needs `note`. A last resort: prefer `requires`.                                                                  |
| `note`           | `text`      | Why the case is limited to `harnesses`. The report shows it.                                                                                                                                      |
| `tags`           | `tags`      | Labels for selecting cases with `--tag`, `--tag-all` and `--not-tag`. Each is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.                                                                              |
| `description`    | `text`      | What the case shows, in a sentence.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `targets`        | `texts`     | The names of the skills the case is about. The report counts the cases of each in its coverage table.                                                                                             |
| `kind`           | `text`      | The kind of case, such as `trigger` or `negative`.                                                                                                                                                |
| `expected`       | `text`      | What a good run does, in a sentence. It is for readers; no check reads it.                                                                                                                        |
| `guard`          | `bool`      | True for a case that must keep passing. The report lists it in its own table. Its score counts in the suite score like any other. Default: false.                                                 |
| `reps`           | `int`       | Runs for each subject in this case, in place of `--reps`.                                                                                                                                         |
| `model`          | `text`      | The model of the agent in this case, in place of `--model`.                                                                                                                                       |
| `judgeModel`     | `text`      | The model that scores the judged checks of this case, in place of `--judge-model`.                                                                                                                |
| `env`            | `envvars`   | Variables the agent's process gets, with the values given here. A name starts with `CASE_`, or is `TZ`, `LANG` or `LC_ALL`.                                                                       |
| `minDelta`       | `signed`    | The least score difference, B minus A, that the case must show. A number from -1 to 1; a negative number lets B score lower by at most that much.                                                 |
| `variants`       | `variants`  | A non-empty list of variants: the same case put differently, such as a paraphrase or a pressure. Each runs as `<case id>@<variant id>`, and the case never runs bare. See the variant keys below. |

## Variant keys

The keys of an object in the `variants` list. A variant needs `id` and exactly one of `prompt` and `promptAppend`. Any other key is a load error, except a key that starts with `x-`. See [Organise a suite](../guides/organise-a-suite.md#variants).

| Key            | Type   | Holds                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | `slug` | The variant's name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique within the case. The case runs as `<case id>@<id>`. |
| `prompt`       | `text` | The whole prompt of the variant, in place of `prompt.md`. Give this or `promptAppend`, not both.                      |
| `promptAppend` | `text` | Text added to the case's `prompt.md` after a blank line. Needs a `prompt.md`. Give this or `prompt`, not both.        |
| `heldout`      | `bool` | True for a variant that runs only with `--heldout`, so that tuning a skill does not see it. Default: false.           |
| `tags`         | `tags` | Tags added to the case's tags for this variant.                                                                       |

## Tool kinds

A `kind` is one of these words.

| Kind       | Meaning                                                              |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shell`    | Ran a command.                                                       |
| `read`     | Read a file.                                                         |
| `write`    | Created or replaced a file.                                          |
| `edit`     | Changed part of a file, or deleted one.                              |
| `search`   | Searched or listed files.                                            |
| `web`      | Fetched a page or searched the web.                                  |
| `skill`    | Called the harness's skill tool.                                     |
| `subagent` | Started another agent.                                               |
| `other`    | Any tool the harness's adapter has no kind for, such as an MCP tool. |
